WEBVTT

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:021
<v Roman>Hi Alice, thanks for joining. I wanted to use this session to lock down the migration scope and timeline.</v>

00:00:22.000 --> 00:00:035
<v Alice Johnson>Sure. From our side the biggest priority is moving the customer records without disrupting the sales team's daily work.</v>

00:00:35.000 --> 00:00:048
<v Mark Wilson>And we need the reporting dashboards to keep working during the transition. We don't want a gap in reporting.</v>

00:00:48.000 --> 00:01:003
<v Roman>Understood. We can run the old and new systems in parallel for the first two weeks. That gives us a rollback option.</v>

00:01:04.000 --> 00:01:014
<v Alice Johnson>That works. What do you need from our team before the first migration?</v>

00:01:14.000 --> 00:01:027
<v Roman>A cleaned export of the customer data and one person from your team to validate the migrated records.</v>

00:01:27.000 --> 00:01:040
<v Mark Wilson>I can own the validation. We also have some duplicate records that should probably be cleaned before migration.</v>

00:01:41.000 --> 00:01:050
<v Roman>Good point. We'll include a duplicate check in the preparation phase.</v>

00:01:50.000 --> 00:01:058
<v Alice Johnson>Then I'm comfortable with the timeline you sent yesterday.</v>

00:01:58.000 --> 00:02:010
<v Roman>Great. I'll send the final implementation plan and we'll start with the data preparation next Monday.</v>

WEBVTT

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:022
<v Roman>Thanks for making time. Today I'd like to get more specific about the analytics use cases and the commercial expectations.</v>

00:00:23.000 --> 00:00:036
<v David Miller>The main thing we want is a dashboard that shows revenue, customer activity, and pipeline movement in one place.</v>

00:00:36.000 --> 00:00:047
<v Emily Davis>We also need filters by region and product. Our current reports are too manual.</v>

00:00:47.000 --> 00:00:058
<v Roman>That's all supported. The question is volume. How many users do you expect initially?</v>

00:00:59.000 --> 00:01:008
<v David Miller>Around 120 users, with maybe another 80 over the next year.</v>

00:01:08.000 --> 00:01:022
<v Roman>Okay. That changes the pricing tier slightly. I can prepare a revised proposal based on 120 users and projected growth.</v>

00:01:22.000 --> 00:01:033
<v Emily Davis>Please also separate implementation from the recurring license. Procurement needs those as separate line items.</v>

00:01:34.000 --> 00:01:041
<v Roman>Absolutely. I'll make that distinction clear.</v>

00:01:41.000 --> 00:01:053
<v David Miller>If the revised pricing is reasonable, we should be able to move to the commercial review.</v>

00:01:53.000 --> 00:02:004
<v Roman>I'll send the revised proposal tomorrow and we can review it in the next meeting.</v>

WEBVTT

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:020
<v Brock>Let's start with the migration scope. Sophia, can you walk us through the current data sources?</v>

00:00:21.000 --> 00:00:031
<v Sophia Moore>We have the CRM, billing system, support platform, and two legacy databases.</v>

00:00:31.000 --> 00:00:044
<v Michael Taylor>The legacy databases are the difficult part. Their schemas are inconsistent and there are a lot of historical records.</v>

00:00:44.000 --> 00:00:053
<v Brock>How much history do you actually need in the new warehouse?</v>

00:00:54.000 --> 00:01:003
<v Sophia Moore>Seven years for finance and three years for operational reporting.</v>

00:01:03.000 --> 00:01:016
<v Brock>That is manageable. We'll archive the older operational data rather than loading all of it into the active warehouse.</v>

00:01:16.000 --> 00:01:026
<v Michael Taylor>What about validation? We need confidence that the totals match the source systems.</v>

00:01:27.000 --> 00:01:038
<v Brock>We'll create reconciliation checks for record counts and key financial totals at every migration stage.</v>

00:01:38.000 --> 00:01:047
<v Sophia Moore>Good. Can you put those checks into the implementation plan?</v>

00:01:47.000 --> 00:01:057
<v Brock>Yes. I'll add them along with the migration phases and target dates.</v>

WEBVTT

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:021
<v Brock>Daniel, before we talk about the final proposal, I want to understand the security concerns you raised in email.</v>

00:00:22.000 --> 00:00:035
<v Daniel Thomas>The main issue is data isolation. We need confirmation that one customer can never access another customer's data.</v>

00:00:35.000 --> 00:00:045
<v Olivia Martin>We also need audit logs for administrative actions and a documented retention policy.</v>

00:00:45.000 --> 00:00:055
<v Brock>Both are supported. We can provide tenant-level isolation and immutable audit records.</v>

00:00:56.000 --> 00:01:008
<v Daniel Thomas>We need that in writing. Our security team won't approve the purchase based on a verbal confirmation.</v>

00:01:08.000 --> 00:01:016
<v Brock>That's fair. I'll send the architecture and security documentation.</v>

00:01:16.000 --> 00:01:027
<v Olivia Martin>There's also a pricing concern. The current proposal is above the budget we approved.</v>

00:01:28.000 --> 00:01:039
<v Brock>Is the budget fixed, or is there flexibility if we reduce the initial scope?</v>

00:01:39.000 --> 00:01:047
<v Daniel Thomas>The budget is effectively fixed for this year.</v>

00:01:47.000 --> 00:02:000
<v Brock>Understood. I'll see what we can do, but I don't want to promise a number before checking internally.</v>

00:02:01.000 --> 00:02:013
<v Daniel Thomas>Then let's pause the commercial decision until we have the security documents and a revised option.</v>

00:02:13.000 --> 00:02:023
<v Brock>Agreed. I'll send the documentation first and follow up with a revised proposal.</v>

WEBVTT

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:021
<v Brock>Thanks everyone. I want to use this meeting for the final review before we move the portal into implementation.</v>

00:00:22.000 --> 00:00:033
<v William Jackson>The latest build looks good. The login and account-management flows are working as expected.</v>

00:00:33.000 --> 00:00:047
<v Emma White>We tested the support workflow too. The only change we requested was adding a confirmation message after submitting a request.</v>

00:00:47.000 --> 00:00:055
<v Brock>That can be included without changing the delivery date.</v>

00:00:56.000 --> 00:01:002
<v William Jackson>What about the launch process?</v>

00:01:02.000 --> 00:01:015
<v Brock>We'll do a controlled rollout first, monitor errors for 24 hours, and then open it to all users.</v>

00:01:15.000 --> 00:01:024
<v Emma White>That sounds reasonable. Do you need anything else from us?</v>

00:01:25.000 --> 00:01:035
<v Brock>Just the final list of production users and the support escalation contacts.</v>

00:01:35.000 --> 00:01:041
<v William Jackson>We'll send those today.</v>

00:01:41.000 --> 00:01:051
<v Brock>Perfect. Once we have those, I'll mark the project ready for implementation.</v>

WEBVTT

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:018
<v Steve>Charlotte, I'd like to focus today on transaction volume and the commercial terms.</v>

00:00:19.000 --> 00:00:028
<v Charlotte Lee>Our expected volume is around 1.5 million transactions per month initially.</v>

00:00:28.000 --> 00:00:037
<v Henry Lewis>And we'd like the pricing to step down as volume increases.</v>

00:00:37.000 --> 00:00:047
<v Steve>We can structure volume-based pricing. I need to confirm the exact thresholds internally.</v>

00:00:48.000 --> 00:00:056
<v Charlotte Lee>Our finance team also wants net-45 payment terms.</v>

00:00:56.000 --> 00:01:006
<v Steve>Our standard is net-30, but I can take net-45 back for approval.</v>

00:01:06.000 --> 00:01:017
<v Henry Lewis>If both of those are workable, the technical side is already in good shape.</v>

00:01:18.000 --> 00:01:029
<v Steve>That's helpful. I'll separate the pricing tiers and payment terms in the revised proposal.</v>

00:01:29.000 --> 00:01:037
<v Charlotte Lee>Good. Let's target the commercial review for next week.</v>

00:01:37.000 --> 00:01:045
<v Steve>Agreed. I'll send the updated proposal before then.</v>

WEBVTT

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:018
<v Steve>Thanks for joining. Today is the final scope review for the mobile application.</v>

00:00:19.000 --> 00:00:029
<v Amelia Hall>We reviewed the latest build and the core booking flow is correct.</v>

00:00:29.000 --> 00:00:041
<v Alexander Walker>We also tested notifications. There was one issue with delayed push notifications, but it appears fixed.</v>

00:00:41.000 --> 00:00:049
<v Steve>Good. Are there any remaining blockers from your side?</v>

00:00:50.000 --> 00:01:000
<v Amelia Hall>No blockers. We'd like analytics events for booking, cancellation, and payment confirmation.</v>

00:01:00.000 --> 00:01:008
<v Steve>Those events are already in the implementation plan.</v>

00:01:08.000 --> 00:01:014
<v Alexander Walker>What is the deployment sequence?</v>

00:01:15.000 --> 00:01:028
<v Steve>We'll deploy to the internal test group first, then a small percentage of production users, and expand after monitoring.</v>

00:01:28.000 --> 00:01:034
<v Amelia Hall>That works for us.</v>

00:01:34.000 --> 00:01:044
<v Steve>Great. I'll mark the scope as approved and send the deployment checklist.</v>

WEBVTT

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:019
<v Kurt>Harper, thanks for joining. I want to close the remaining questions around enterprise licensing.</v>

00:00:20.000 --> 00:00:032
<v Harper Young>The functionality looks right. The open question is the annual price at our expected user count.</v>

00:00:32.000 --> 00:00:042
<v Matthew Allen>We also need the enterprise security terms reviewed by our legal team.</v>

00:00:42.000 --> 00:00:055
<v Kurt>We can provide the security documentation today. For pricing, what user count should I use for the final proposal?</v>

00:00:56.000 --> 00:01:007
<v Harper Young>Around 600 users initially, with a possibility of 900 by the end of the year.</v>

00:01:07.000 --> 00:01:018
<v Kurt>Okay. I'll price the initial commitment at 600 and include the expansion tier separately.</v>

00:01:18.000 --> 00:01:025
<v Matthew Allen>That would help procurement compare the options.</v>

00:01:26.000 --> 00:01:036
<v Kurt>I'll also include the implementation and support costs as separate line items.</v>

00:01:36.000 --> 00:01:047
<v Harper Young>Good. If the numbers are within our range, we can move to legal review.</v>

00:01:47.000 --> 00:01:054
<v Kurt>I'll send the final commercial proposal tomorrow.</v>

WEBVTT

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:018
<v Kurt>Evelyn, I'd like to understand the decision before we close the opportunity.</v>

00:00:19.000 --> 00:00:031
<v Evelyn Wright>The product itself was well received. The issue is the expected return compared with the implementation cost.</v>

00:00:31.000 --> 00:00:043
<v Ethan King>We ran the numbers again after the proposal. We don't think the first-year savings justify the investment.</v>

00:00:43.000 --> 00:00:051
<v Kurt>Would reducing the initial scope change that calculation?</v>

00:00:52.000 --> 00:01:000
<v Evelyn Wright>Possibly, but we'd still have the internal change-management cost.</v>

00:01:00.000 --> 00:01:010
<v Kurt>Understood. If we proposed a smaller pilot, would that be something you'd consider?</v>

00:01:10.000 --> 00:01:020
<v Evelyn Wright>Not right now. We have another initiative competing for the same budget.</v>

00:01:21.000 --> 00:01:028
<v Ethan King>We'd rather revisit this next planning cycle.</v>

00:01:28.000 --> 00:01:041
<v Kurt>That's clear. I'll record the opportunity as closed and note that budget allocation and ROI were the main reasons.</v>

00:01:41.000 --> 00:01:047
<v Evelyn Wright>That accurately reflects our decision.</v>

WEBVTT

00:00:08.000 --> 00:00:021
<v John>Grace, I'll start with a quick overview and then we can focus on the workflows that matter to PeopleFirst.</v>

00:00:22.000 --> 00:00:034
<v Grace Hill>The biggest issue for us is repetitive HR support questions. Employees ask the same things constantly.</v>

00:00:34.000 --> 00:00:045
<v Logan Nelson>We'd like the assistant to answer those questions but escalate anything involving sensitive employee information.</v>

00:00:45.000 --> 00:00:056
<v John>That's a good fit. We can define escalation rules based on topic and confidence.</v>

00:00:57.000 --> 00:01:009
<v Grace Hill>Can it also surface the source of the answer? Our HR team needs to verify policy responses.</v>

00:01:09.000 --> 00:01:018
<v John>Yes. We can include the source document with each response.</v>

00:01:18.000 --> 00:01:026
<v Logan Nelson>What about integration with our existing ticketing system?</v>

00:01:27.000 --> 00:01:040
<v John>We have an API integration for that. Tickets can be created automatically when the assistant escalates a case.</v>

00:01:40.000 --> 00:01:049
<v Grace Hill>That covers our main requirements. We'd like a technical demo next.</v>

00:01:49.000 --> 00:01:058
<v John>I'll schedule the demo and include the ticketing and escalation workflows.</v>
